minutes.headline: Sewer Commission adopted new grease trap rules, approved the CWMP update for town meeting, and chose sealed bids for the operations contract.
minutes.summary: The commission held hearings on a bylaw article for regulation-change procedure, new grease trap and interceptor regulations, and the comprehensive wastewater management plan update. It then heard a manhole inspection update, handled the Twin City waiver and betterment reassessment, and chose the invitation-for-bid route for the operations contract.

public_comment.topic: Resident asked the commission to explain the sewer department's finances, citing a figure heard at the selectmen's meeting.
Asked about starting fees on July 1 and what a waiver on an external grease trap means.
Supported the grease regulation changes so homeowners do not pay for business grease.
Resident asked about the number of grease traps, revenue and cost, seasonality, and effective dates.
Resident asked what her betterment would cost and when it would appear on taxes.
Resident questioned betterment estimates and the Rolling Acres pressure units.

votes.motion: Close the hearing on the sewer regulation changes.
Finalize and release the grease trap regulation change.
Accept the updated CWMP dated April 2016 with the discussed additions and take it to town meeting.
Use the invitation for bid process for the next operations and maintenance contract.
Approve the invitation for bid with transitional support at the contract rate table.
Reassess the Twin City betterment from one parcel to the correct parcel.

budget_items.what_was_said: Fees move to a two-tier structure, with separate fees for internal and external traps, depending on compliance.
Updated cost estimates by service area, ranging from about 19,000 to 60,000 per unit.
Chair said no operating funds are set aside for pump replacement, with retained earnings available.
Chair compared Lemonster and Fitchburg treatment rates and the blended sewer rate.
Invoices from Fitchburg and Wright Pierce for the CWMP, Lake View and manhole project; the state grant pays most of the manhole cost.
A remaining betterment balance is moved to the correct parcel.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted to accept the April 2016 update of the comprehensive wastewater management plan, with the discussed additions, and take it to town meeting.
The commission voted to finalize and release the grease trap regulation change, after a hearing that also drew public questions on fees and timing.
The commission voted to use the invitation-for-bid process for the next operations and maintenance contract, then approved the bid with transitional support at the contract rate table.
The commission voted to reassess a Twin City betterment from one parcel to the correct parcel.
The Twin City waiver request was referred: staff are to ask for the plumbing inspector's sign-off before any waiver is granted.

why_it_matters: The grease trap rules move permit fees to a two-tier structure for internal and external traps, which can change what food businesses pay and is meant to keep grease costs off homeowners' sewer bills.
The wastewater plan going to town meeting carries betterment estimates by service area, so residents may be asked to vote on a plan that leads to betterment charges on property tax bills.
Bidding the operations contract sets who runs the sewer system and at what rate, which feeds into future sewer rates.
watch_next: The wastewater management plan update at town meeting.
Staff follow-up on the Twin City plumbing inspector sign-off before the waiver is granted.
